decisions.reason: The audience-comprehension criterion does not change which source footage is permitted or required.
Requiring an unfamiliar viewer to understand the clip does not change the existing white-text, font, or caption-effects rules.
The standalone comprehension criterion does not alter the independently specified clean-editing, animation, or transition rules.
Audience comprehension does not change the existing 45-to-60-second duration requirement.
The source adds a standalone audience-comprehension criterion to moment completeness, but it does not change the separate standard for selecting strong and impactful source moments.
The clip comprehension standard does not change the Lead Clipper pathway, training, compensation, or responsibilities.
The audience-comprehension rule does not change the publishing destination, approval prerequisite, or current batch publication schedule.
The content-comprehension criterion does not alter the batch size, deadline, folder naming, link access, or submission channel.
The five-clip production instruction and comprehension standard do not revise the previously completed qualification method or success gate.
The current five-clip batch and its audience-comprehension standard do not change the 100-approved-clips monthly quota or counting rule.
Audience comprehension becomes a clip-quality criterion, but the approval authority, publication eligibility, and rejected-clip handling remain unchanged.
